blocks.text: High-rise buildings and a green spiral tower in Panama City, Panama
Panama City’s modern skyline and the tower with a spiralling façade

After breakfast, head to El Valle de Antón, also known as Antón Valley. The town sits inside the caldera of the El Valle de Antón stratovolcano. The caldera has a radius of about 6 km and formed approximately 1.1–1.3 million years ago. People first settled here several thousand years ago, and today there is a town inside the crater.

After busy Panama City, the valley feels quieter, with low-rise buildings, greenery, mountains and a mild climate. Temperatures average around 28 °C during the day and 20 °C at night, with little seasonal variation.

One of the main stops is the Central Market. Stalls sell vegetables, fruit, flowers, orchids, souvenirs and local crafts. Sundays are especially lively, when people come in from nearby villages. Look for pottery, wooden tableware and carvings, soapstone crafts, local coconut sweets and jewellery made with semiprecious stones found in the surrounding mountains.

The area’s history is tied to the Indigenous Guaymí people, who lived here before Europeans arrived.

A local legend tells of the mountain known as La India Dormida, or the Sleeping Indian Woman. Its silhouette has become a symbol of El Valle and often appears on souvenirs.

Another stop is Chorro del Macho, a waterfall about 70 m high.

**Canopy zipline above Chorro del Macho waterfall**

**Canopy tour:** available at an additional cost.

Downstream, you can swim in a natural pool with flowing water at 26–28 °C.

During the day, you’ll also visit El Níspero, a private zoo and botanical garden.

**Lunch:** the excursion price does not include lunch. Your guide can recommend local restaurants.  
**Canopy tour:** available at an additional cost.
